sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Rusia 1.

Petitioner has filed this present petition challenging the Award dated 25.8.2025 passed by the Additional Collector & Arbitrator, District Indore, under Section 3G(5) of the National Highway Authority of India Act (in short "NHAI Act"), whereby the application filed under Section 3G(5) has been dismissed and the award dated 16.3.2021 and Amended Award dated 19.12.2023 have been affirmed.

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner cannot be relegated to the appellate forum.
4. Shri Dave, the Deputy Solicitor General, opposes the above submissions.
We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5. In order to meet out the aforesaid contention, it is necessary to examine the facts of the present case.

6. The petitioner became a co-owner of the land bearing Survey Nos. 464/1, 464/2/1, and 465/2/1/3, with a total area of 0.046 hectare (5000 sq. feet), by virtue of the sale deed executed between Prafulla Kumar Sharma and Smt. Anju Garg i.e. petitioner.
Before execution of the sale deed, the entire land was got diverted by the owner.
By way of the aforesaid sale deed, the petitioner purchased a plot of 5000 sq.ft.
Apart from the petitioner, 14 others also purchased the similar size of plots.
It means a big land was divided into plots by way of illegal colonisation without sanction of a development plan by the T&CP.
Thereafter, the petitioner applied for mutation, and vide order dated 21.8.2025, her name was directed to be mutated as the owner of the 5000 sq.ft. plot.
The petitioner started paying the revenue to the government.

7. A part of land of various survey numbers of Gram Datoda was NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2 0 2 5 : M P H C - I N D : 3 2 2 3 2 3 W P - 4 1 2 4 5 - 2 0 2 5 a c q u i r e d u n d e r t h e N H A I A c t f o r widening/construction of National Highway No.347 BG (Indore-Aedalabad Block).
The Land Acquisition Officer (CALA) passed an award dated 16.3.2021.
The petitioner and other co-owners did not find their names in the award, therefore, the petitioner submitted an objection to the collector.
The enquiry was directed to be conducted, in which a report was submitted that the petitioner and 14 others purchased plots from F-1 to F-19 in the AG Resorts.
The demarcation of the plots was carried out.
The petitioner was found in possession of Plot No.F-8.

In view of the aforesaid report, the award dated 16.3.2021 came to be modified by the CALA vide award dated 19.12.2023,
ascertaining the share of the petitioner for acquisition of her 5000 sq.ft. land in the total compensation payable to the erstwhile owner .
8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, the petitioner preferred an application under Section 3G(5) of the NHAI Act before the Additional Collector.

Therefore, once the petitioner has challenged the amended award by way of an application under Section 3G(5) of the NHAI Act, now she cannot be permitted to deviate from the regular remedy of Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act available under the NHAI Act.

9. It seems that the petitioner purchased a piece of land admeasuring 5000 sq.ft. from a developer/owner of the total land of Patwari Halka No. 25 Survey No. 464/1, 464/4, 464/2/1,
465/2, 465/2/1/3.

The land-owner developed the AG Resorts and sold the plots to various persons,
including the petitioner.

Nothing is mentioned in the sale deed of the petitioner about the approved plan by the Town and Country Planning Department, which NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:32232 4 WP-41245-2025 amounts to an illegal colonisation.

sentences.text: There is no division of plots in the revenue record by way of Batankan, therefore, the NHAI could not recognize the independent status of the petitioner.
Now at the instance of the petitioner, the entire land acquisition proceedings cannot be quashed by entertaining this writ petition, as she is one of the purchasers of the illegal colony.
Now at this stage the petitioner can only challenge the award or amended award for enhancement of compensation by way of application under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
The ownership of the petitioner of the land, which has been acquired, is not in dispute in this case, hence the petitioner can only seek enhancement of compensation.
10. The petition is dismissed with the aforesaid liberty.
